To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) users can intuitively express shape deformation by using the geometric properties of their hand and (b) the geometric properties of a hand can be used to model the shaping process of a pot

the geometry of the contact between the hand of a user and the object being shaped can be used to infer the user’s intent for shape deformation, and this approach enables users to express their design intent without the need for any pre-defined hand gestures.
it is possible for users to express their design intent in virtual pottery by manipulating the geometry of the pot’s surface with their hands and fingers.

the question of whether the geometry of contact can be used to express the intent for shape deformation.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have demonstrated a new geometric approach for midair expression of design intent for 3D virtual shaping, without requiring the user to learn, know or remember a fixed set of hand gestures.
our results show that the geometry of hand-shape can be used to express design intent in virtual shaping processes.
our results suggest the feasibility of a gesture-free geometric approach to mid-air expression of intent during a shaping process, and that this approach is intuitive and effective for users.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that it is possible for the user to express the intent for a shaping operation in virtual pottery by the geometry of contact alone.
we show that the geometry of hand-shape and contact can be used to enable users to interact with virtual shapes without the need for pre-defined gestures.
we show that a user’s hand shape is an expressive medium that can be used to convey design intent for virtual shaping processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a user’s intent for shaping a virtual pot can be expressed by a geometric relationship between the hand and pot, which can then be used to control the shape of the pot.

the geometry of the hand and its contact with a shape can provide a sufficient basis to enable users to interactively express design intent in shaping processes without requiring the user to learn, remember, or use gestures.

it is possible for a user to convey their intent for a shape deformation without the use of any gestures, and that such an intent can be captured from the contact geometry between the user’s hand and the object being manipulated.
